'''Aaron Michael Gray''' (born December 7, 1984) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played seven seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). A heart condition forced him into early retirement in 2015.

==Early life and education==
Gray was born December 7, 1984, in the [[Tarzana, Los Angeles|Tarzana]] section of [[Los Angeles]], California, and attended [[Emmaus High School]] in [[Emmaus, Pennsylvania]].

==High school career==
Gray played [[high school basketball]] for [[Emmaus High School]], which is a member of Pennsylvania's highly competitive [[Eastern Pennsylvania Conference|East Penn Conference]]. Gray did not begin playing for the varsity team until the middle of his sophomore season. In Gray's senior season at Emmaus High School, he was named Pennsylvania's [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]].

Gray was recruited by major collegiate basketball programs, including [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]], [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pitt]], and [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]], and committed to Pitt.

==College career==
While at [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pitt]], Gray was named a Third Team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] after helping lead Pitt to the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|Sweet 16]] in the [[2007 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2007 NCAA Division I tournament]] in March 2007.

==National Basketball Association==
{{Further|2007 NBA draft}}
At the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]'s pre-draft camp in 2007, Gray was the only player whose height measured at least seven feet without shoes.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2007 Draft Combine {{!}} Pre Draft camp Measurements {{!}} 2007 NBA Draft|url=http://www.mynbadraft.com/2007-nba-draft-combine-measurements|access-date=2020-10-27|website=www.mynbadraft.com}}</ref> He was selected with the 49th overall selection by the [[Chicago Bulls]] in the [[2007 NBA draft]].

===Chicago Bulls (2007–2010)===
On November 2, 2007, Gray made his NBA debut with the [[Chicago Bulls]] against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. On April 16, 2008, against the [[Toronto Raptors]], he recorded 19 points, 22 rebounds, and two assists in 35 minutes of play.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080421002302/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280416004 Bulls beat Raptors as Toronto barely uses starters]</ref> In the [[2007–08 Chicago Bulls season|2007–08 season]], Gray scored 262 points and recorded 168 rebounds for the Bulls.

===New Orleans Hornets (2010–2011)===
On January 25, 2010, the Bulls traded Gray to the [[New Orleans Pelicans|New Orleans Hornets]] for [[Devin Brown]].<ref>{{cite web | title = HORNETS ACQUIRE AARON GRAY FROM BULLS | url = http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_acquire_aaron_gray_fro_2010_01_25.html | work = NBA.com | date = 2010-01-25 | access-date = 2010-01-25}}</ref>

On July 15, 2010, the Hornets re-signed Gray.<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=6237 Hornets re-sign Aaron Gray]</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2011–2013)===
On December 11, 2011, Gray was signed to a one-year contract by the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Raptors sign center Aaron Gray | url = http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=8781 | work = InsideHoops.com | date = December 11, 2011 | access-date = March 2, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = Raptors Sign Free-Agent Centre Aaron Gray | url = http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/20111211/21941/raptors-sign-free-agent-centre-aaron-gray | work = NBA.com | date = December 11, 2011 | access-date = March 2, 2013}}</ref>

On July 27, 2012, Gray was re-signed by the Raptors.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/2012/news/07/27/raptors-lucas.ap/index.html Raptors re-sign Gray, ink free-agent guard Lucas III] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120731000253/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/07/27/raptors-lucas.ap/index.html |date=2012-07-31 }}</ref>

On January 28, 2013, Gray recorded a career high 22 points, along with 10 rebounds, in a 114–102 loss to [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20130128/GSWTOR/gameinfo.html Notebook: Warriors 114, Raptors 102]</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2013–2014)===
On December 9, 2013, the Raptors traded Gray, [[Rudy Gay]], and [[Quincy Acy]], to the [[Sacramento Kings]] for [[Greivis Vásquez]], [[Patrick Patterson (basketball)|Patrick Patterson]], [[John Salmons]], and [[Chuck Hayes]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-rudy-gay-quincy-acy-and-aaron-gray-toronto|title=Kings Acquire Rudy Gay, Quincy Acy and Aaron Gray from Toronto|work=NBA.com|date=December 9, 2013|access-date=December 9, 2013}}</ref>

===Detroit Pistons (2014)===
On August 18, 2014, Gray signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/pistons-sign-free-agent-forward-cartier-martin-and-center-aaron-gray Pistons Sign Free Agent Forward Cartier Martin and Center Aaron Gray]</ref> On September 29, 2014, the Pistons announced Gray would miss training camp while rehabbing from a cardiac episode suffered following a voluntary workout in late August.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-center-aaron-gray-out-indefinitely Detroit Pistons Center Aaron Gray Out Indefinitely]</ref> On October 26, 2014, he was waived by the Pistons.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/10/26/pistons-waive-gray/index.html |title=Pistons waive center Aaron Gray |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2014-10-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141028144129/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/10/26/pistons-waive-gray/index.html |archive-date=2014-10-28 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On June 19, 2015, Gray retired after a [[Thrombus|blood clot]] was discovered in his heart in the summer of 2014.<ref name="retire">{{cite news |url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2015/06/19/detroit-pistons-aaron-gray/29001109/ |title=Aaron Gray stays upbeat after blood clot forces retirement |last=Ellis |first=Vince |newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=June 19, 2015 |access-date=June 19, 2015}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
=== Detroit Pistons (2015–2018) ===
Following the end of his playing career, Gray joined [[Stan Van Gundy]]'s staff with the [[Detroit Pistons]] as an assistant coach to work with the team's big men and with young prospects of the [[Grand Rapids Drive]], team's [[NBA G League]].<ref name="retire"/>
